question: What is the term for a piece of dead bone that breaks away from healthy bone during an infection like osteomyelitis?
explanation: A sequestrum is a piece of dead, avascular bone that gets walled off from living bone tissue during an infection. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h1)

question: Why does swelling inside an infected bone lead to bone tissue death?

options.A: It squashes local blood vessels and cuts off the oxygen supply
options.B: It directly activates bone-dissolving cells across the entire matrix
options.C: It pushes bacteria through the bone canals at high speeds
options.D: It causes the bone marrow to instantly turn into scar tissue

explanation: Because bone is rigid and cannot expand, swelling raises the internal pressure, which cuts off blood flow and causes tissue death. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h1)

question: Which sign points more toward chronic osteomyelitis rather than an acute case?

options.A: Rapid destruction of the nearby joint
options.D: Sudden high fever and severe shivering

explanation: Chronic osteomyelitis often features sinus tracts that continuously or periodically drain pus out to the skin. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h2)

question: What kind of pain does a patient with acute osteomyelitis typically feel in the affected bone?

options.A: Sharp pain that disappears completely when you touch the skin
options.B: Cramping muscle pain that goes away with a gentle leg massage
options.C: Deep, constant, throbbing pain that gets worse when they move
options.D: Burning surface pain brought on by cold air

explanation: The high pressure inside the bone creates a deep, constant, throbbing ache that intensifies when the limb moves. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h2)

question: Why might a regular X-ray look totally normal during the first week of an acute bone infection?

options.A: A lot of bone mineral must be lost before it shows up on an X-ray
options.B: X-rays only show soft tissue and cannot pass through bone
options.C: Inflammatory fluid absorbs all the radiation
options.D: Bacterial toxins temporarily stop the X-ray machine from working

explanation: About thirty to fifty percent of bone structure must be lost before damage becomes visible on a standard X-ray. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which imaging test is best for spotting bone marrow inflammation earliest?
explanation: MRI can show changes in soft tissues and bone marrow long before bone destruction appears on a standard X-ray. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h3)

question: How long do patients typically need intravenous antibiotics to treat osteomyelitis effectively?
explanation: Bone infections need a long course of antibiotics to completely clear the bacteria from areas with poor blood supply. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h4)

question: Why are intravenous antibiotics usually chosen at the start of osteomyelitis treatment?

options.A: It means nurses do not need to check lab values
options.B: It delivers high levels of medicine to areas of bone with poor blood flow
options.C: It completely prevents any stomach upset
options.D: It cures the infection within a day without surgery

explanation: Giving drugs directly into the vein ensures high blood levels so the medicine can reach infected, hard-to-penetrate bone tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement when treating osteomyelitis?

options.A: To permanently fuse the nearby joint space
options.B: To permanently seal all skin incisions shut
options.C: To remove infected and dead bone tissue
options.D: To replace bone marrow with a synthetic gel

explanation: Debridement physically removes dead bone and infected material that antibiotics alone cannot reach. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h5)

question: Why might a surgeon use a muscle flap over a bone cleanup site?

options.A: To seal the skin so dressings never need changing
options.B: To permanently replace missing joint cartilage
options.C: To immediately make the limb stronger for weight-bearing
options.D: To bring in a fresh blood supply that helps antibiotics and healing reach the area

explanation: Muscle flaps bring a fresh blood supply to scarred, poorly healed areas, helping clear leftover infection and speed up recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h5)

question: Which dietary focus is most important when caring for a patient recovering from osteomyelitis?

options.A: High protein and vitamins to support tissue healing
options.B: Strict fluid restriction to reduce local swelling
options.C: Low calorie intake to prevent weight gain
options.D: High carbohydrate diet for quick energy

explanation: Cell repair and a strong immune system require plenty of protein and key vitamins. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is a crucial instruction for a patient going home with a long-term intravenous antibiotic plan?

options.A: Finish the entire course of medicine even if you feel completely better
options.B: Switch to oral pills as soon as your fever stops for a day
options.C: Flush your central line with plain tap water daily
options.D: Stop taking the pills right away if you feel slightly tired

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early often causes the bone infection to return and can lead to drug-resistant bacteria. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h6)
